scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kummattikali is a traditional folk dance rooted in the Malabar region of Kerala, specifically within the Thrissur and Palakkad districts.
It is categorized as a devotional ritual art form, often linked to Shaiva mythology.
The 'pristine' or original version of the dance is historically associated with the Bhadrakali temple in Palakkad.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Kummattikali is performed during the Onam festival.
It is a devotional act intended to please deities, classified as a ritualistic art form.
The character of Thamma represents the mother of all beings, lending a spiritual depth to the performance.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves performers moving in a procession from house to house.
The movement is characterized by the manipulation of long agricultural sticks called Kummattikali.
The troupe is led by a character named Thamma, who portrays an old woman walking with a stick.
Watch for Thamma's Walk.

Formation: Processional movement through village streets and house courtyards

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary musical accompaniment is the Onavillu, a bow-like instrument made from areca nut wood.
The sound is produced by beating the strings of the bow with a narrow bamboo stick, creating a vibrating rhythmic foundation.
Listen for the Onavillu (areca nut wood bow), Bamboo stick.

The sound is dominated by the unique, resonant vibration of the Onavillu, a wooden bow whose string is struck to create a rhythmic drone. This is accompanied by the chanting or singing of mythological verses.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The costume is the most distinctive element, featuring masks carved from woods like jackfruit, Hog Plum, or Coral tree.
These masks depict characters like Krishna, Narada, or hunters, often featuring a 'talla' (toothless mouth).
The dancers' bodies are covered in skirts of plaited grass or bunches of grass to create a bushy appearance.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The sources do not name individual historical dancers, but they highlight specific mythological figures portrayed: Krishna, Narada, Kiratha, Darika, and the central character Thamma (the old woman).
The dance is prevalent in Thrissur and Palakkad districts.
Kummattikali belongs to the devotional category of Kerala's ritualistic folk arts.

visual_brief.costume_notes: The costume is the most distinctive element, featuring masks carved from woods like jackfruit, Hog Plum, or Coral tree. These masks depict characters like Krishna, Narada, or hunters, often featuring a 'talla' (toothless mouth). The dancers' bodies are covered in skirts of plaited grass or bunches of grass to create a bushy appearance. The setting is typically the outdoors, moving through village streets and residential courtyards during the Onam festival.
visual_brief.setting_notes: Kummattikali is performed during the Onam festival. It is a devotional act intended to please deities, classified as a ritualistic art form. The character of Thamma represents the mother of all beings, lending a spiritual depth to the performance. The act of moving from house to house to collect rice and jaggery reinforces communal bonds and celebrates the harvest season.
